questions.question: A sign at the PNE says that six thousand four hundred five people visited the fair on Saturday. Which number is that in standard form?
questions.explain: Word form names the thousands, hundreds, tens and ones in order: 6 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens, 5 ones gives 6 405. The trap is that no tens are said out loud, so you must still write a 0 in the tens place — leaving it out makes 645, and sliding the 5 over makes 6 450.

questions.question: A ferry from Tsawwassen carried 4 738 passengers in one day. What is the value of the digit 7 in 4 738?
questions.explain: Find the place the digit sits in: in 4 738 the 7 is in the hundreds place, so its value is 7 hundreds, or 700. The common trap is reading the digit by itself and saying just 7 — a digit's value always depends on its place, not on the digit alone.

questions.question: Leo skip-counts by 25s while stacking quarters: 1 350, 1 375, 1 400, ___. What number comes next?
questions.explain: Counting by 25s means adding 25 each time, so 1 400 + 25 = 1 425. A common slip is to jump by 50 right after a hundred (giving 1 450) or to add only 5 or 15 because the tens digit changed — check by seeing that each step in the pattern is exactly 25.

questions.question: Four Surrey schools collected books for a book drive: 3 090 books, 3 909 books, 3 099 books, and 3 900 books. Which list puts them in order from least to greatest?
questions.explain: Compare place by place from the left: all four have 3 thousands, so look at the hundreds (0, 0, 9, 9), then the tens and ones to break the ties. Two traps here are ordering from greatest to least by mistake, and thinking 3 099 is smaller than 3 090 just because it ends in bigger digits.

questions.question: A Whistler ski hill sold 4 862 lift tickets in one week. Rounded to the nearest hundred, about how many tickets is that?
questions.explain: To round to the nearest hundred, look at the tens digit: 6 is 5 or more, so 4 862 moves up to 4 900. The usual traps are rounding to the wrong place — 4 860 is the nearest ten and 5 000 is the nearest thousand — so always name the place you are rounding to first.

questions.question: Two salmon counts were recorded: 4 872 fish in one river and 7 248 fish in another. How much greater is the value of the digit 4 in 4 872 than the value of the digit 4 in 7 248?
options: The values are equal, because it is the same digit 4
questions.explain: The 4 in 4 872 is in the thousands place (4 000) and the 4 in 7 248 is in the tens place (40), so the difference is 4 000 − 40 = 3 960. The biggest misconception is thinking the same digit always has the same value, and a second trap is adding the two values instead of subtracting.

questions.question: A Victoria school collected bottles for three months: 1 480 in September, 2 610 in October, and 3 250 in November. If each month is rounded to the nearest thousand first, what is the estimated total?
questions.explain: Round each month to the nearest thousand — 1 480 goes to 1 000 (480 is less than 500), 2 610 goes to 3 000, and 3 250 goes to 3 000 — then add: 1 000 + 3 000 + 3 000 = 7 000. Two traps are rounding every number up out of habit (8 000) and rounding to the nearest hundred instead of the nearest thousand (7 400).

questions.question: Noah has $850 saved and adds $25 every week from his paper route. He needs $1 000 for a new bike. How many more weeks until he has enough?
questions.explain: First find the gap, $1 000 − $850 = $150, then skip-count by 25s to cover it: 875, 900, 925, 950, 975, 1 000 — that is 6 weeks. Common traps are counting the starting $850 as one of the jumps and stopping a week early, or skip-counting by 10s instead of 25s and getting 15.
